entries.definition: to send something through the air with the hand
to throw something with great force
to throw something quickly and carelessly

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the single image of throwing and show how each phrase extends it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住「扔」这一个画面，并展示每个搭配如何延伸它。

normal.en: Every sense begins with a hand throwing: a rope, a vote, a shadow, a role or molten metal.
normal.cn: 每个义项都从一只手扔出去开始：绳子、选票、影子、角色或熔融金属。

normal.en: Cast a vote pictures the ballot as a small object thrown into a box.
normal.cn: cast a vote 把选票想象成被扔进箱子的小物件。

normal.en: Cast a shadow keeps the image literal: light throws a dark shape onto the ground.
normal.cn: cast a shadow 保留字面画面：光把一块暗形扔到地面上。

normal.en: The past tense is cast, not casted, so the verb looks unchanged.
normal.cn: 过去式是 cast 而不是 casted，所以动词看起来没有变化。

normal.en: Casting covers both metal and actors because both involve pouring something into a prepared shape.
normal.cn: casting 同时指铸金属和选演员，因为两者都是把东西倒进预备好的形状里。

abstract.en: Picture a fisherman flinging a net in a wide arc.
abstract.cn: 想象渔夫把网甩出一个大弧。

abstract.en: Picture a director pointing at one actor in a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象导演在挤满人的房间里指向一位演员。

abstract.en: Picture sparks flying as hot metal fills a clay mould.
abstract.cn: 想象炽热的金属注入泥模时火星四溅。

examples.en: She cast the line far into the river.
examples.cn: 她把钓线远远抛进河里。

examples.en: The film has a strong cast.
examples.cn: 这部电影的演员阵容很强。

examples.en: The tree cast a cool shadow over the bench.
examples.cn: 那棵树在长椅上投下一片凉影。

dict_mnemonic.text: cast 的核心动作就是「扔」：把绳子扔出去，把票扔进箱，把演员扔进角色，把铁水扔进模具。

root: 源自古诺斯语 kasta（投掷），属日耳曼语词，无拉丁语祖先；由「扔」这一动作扩展出投射、选角与铸造诸义。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing gesture gives the rope, the vote, the shadow, the actor and the molten metal.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个投掷动作先后给出绳子、选票、影子、演员和熔融金属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sending something forward through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西向前甩到空中。

branches.en: The literal throw stays in fishing, dice and ropes.
branches.cn: 字面的扔保留在钓鱼、掷骰和抛绳中。

branches.en: Light thrown from a source lays a shadow down.
branches.cn: 从光源甩出的光把影子放倒在地上。

branches.en: Actors are thrown into parts, and the group of them becomes the cast.
branches.cn: 演员被投进角色，这一群人就成为演员阵容。

branches.en: Molten metal is poured into a mould and hardens into a cast object.
branches.cn: 熔融金属被倒入模具，凝固成铸件。

branches.en: Both keep the force of a deliberate, aimed pour or toss.
branches.cn: 两者都保留了有目标、有力度的倾倒或抛掷感。

intro.en: Cast builds compounds and agent nouns rather than taking classical affixes.
intro.cn: cast 主要构成复合词和表施动者的名词，不常接古典词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: They cast the net at dawn.

items.meaning: the act of shaping or selecting
a metal worker or a small wheel
items.example: The caster lifted the hot mould.
items.exampleCN: 铸工抬起了滚烫的模具。

items.meaning: a statement about what will happen
a hard iron made by casting
items.example: The pan is made of cast iron.

definition_en: a large strong building with thick walls and towers, built to defend a place, or the rook in chess
core_image: 建在高处的石墙与塔楼
scene: 旅行团沿着山路走到一座石砌建筑前。The guide explained how the castle had survived three sieges.
sceneCN: 这里 castle 指「城堡」（第 1 个义项：带厚墙与塔楼的防御建筑）；句意是导游讲解这座城堡如何熬过三次围攻。

senses.title: A fortified stone building
senses.definition: a large building with thick walls, towers and often a moat, built to resist attack
senses.definitionCN: 带厚墙、塔楼，常有护城河，为抵御进攻而建的大型建筑
senses.example: The castle stands on a hill above the town.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡坐落在小镇上方的山丘上。
senses.why: The Latin source was a small fort, and the stone walls and towers grew out of that defensive core.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源词指小要塞，石墙与塔楼正是从这一防御核心长出来的。

senses.title: The rook in chess
senses.definition: one of the two pieces in chess shaped like a tower, moving in straight lines
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中形似塔楼、沿直线行走的两个棋子之一
senses.example: He moved his castle to the open file.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车移到开放线上。
senses.why: The chess piece was carved as a turret, so the tower shape lent its name to the piece.
senses.whyCN: 这枚棋子被雕成小塔楼，于是塔楼的名称就借给了它。

intro.en: Castle descends from a Latin diminutive of a word for fort, and the chess piece borrowed its tower shape.
intro.cn: castle 源自拉丁语中表示要塞的词的指小形式，棋子则借用了它的塔楼外形。

items.en: Castrum meant a fortified camp, and its plural castra named a fort.
items.cn: 拉丁语 castrum 指设防营地，复数 castra 指要塞。

items.en: Castellum, a little fort, is the diminutive that leads to the English word.
items.cn: 指小形式 castellum 意为小要塞，是通向英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Castel enters Old English through Latin and Anglo-Norman French.
items.cn: castel 经拉丁语和盎格鲁诺曼法语进入古英语。

items.en: Castle settles as the word for a nobleman's fortified stone home.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，castle 固定指贵族设防的石砌宅邸。

items.en: The word also names the tower-shaped rook and the sandcastle on the beach.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它也指塔楼形的国际象棋车和沙滩上的沙堡。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the Latin fort root, and the meaning group gathers other strongholds.
note.cn: 形近组留在拉丁语要塞词根内，近义组收其他坚固据点。

entries.definition: the governor of a castle
built with battlements like a castle
a large French country house or castle
a large strong building used for defence
entries.definitionCN: 用于防御的大型坚固建筑

entries.definition: the large official home of a ruler
a tall narrow building or part of one
entries.definitionCN: 高而窄的建筑物或其一部分

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin fort root, the chess shape and the sandcastle image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语要塞词根、棋子的形状和沙堡的画面。

normal.en: The Latin root castrum, a fort, also hides in castellum, the little fort behind castle.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 castrum（要塞）也藏在 castellum 里，后者正是 castle 背后的「小要塞」。

normal.en: The chess castle is simply a tower carved in wood or plastic.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的车不过是一座用木头或塑料雕成的塔楼。

normal.en: Sand castle keeps the word alive on every beach, with walls and towers in miniature.
normal.cn: sand castle 让这个词活在每片沙滩上，用缩小版的墙和塔。

normal.en: Castle in the air means a plan with no foundation, like a castle built on nothing.
normal.cn: castle in the air 指没有根基的计划，就像建在虚空里的城堡。

normal.en: Only the plural castles is needed, since the noun has no verb use here.
normal.cn: 这里只需复数 castles，因为该名词在此没有动词用法。

abstract.en: Picture a grey wall rising above a moat at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时一道灰墙从护城河上方升起。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden tower sliding across a chessboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座木塔在棋盘上滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a child patting wet sand into a tiny turret.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子把湿沙拍成一座小塔。

examples.en: The old castle is open to visitors in summer.
examples.cn: 这座古堡夏天对游客开放。

examples.en: They built a sand castle near the water.
examples.cn: 他们在水边堆了一座沙堡。

examples.en: His plan was a castle in the air.
examples.cn: 他的计划只是空中楼阁。

dict_mnemonic.text: castle 可以想成「卡住」的石头：一层层石头卡在一起，垒成高墙和塔楼。

root: 源自拉丁语 castellum（小要塞），是 castrum（设防营地）的指小形式，经古英语 castel 进入现代拼写。

sensesIntro.en: A small Latin fort grows into a stone home with towers, and its tower shape then names the chess piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁语的小要塞长成带塔楼的石砌宅邸，塔楼外形又给国际象棋的棋子命了名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick stone walls and towers on high ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：高地上的厚石墙与塔楼。

branches.en: Defence stays the first job of the building through the Middle Ages.
branches.cn: 在整个中世纪，防御始终是这座建筑的首要功能。

branches.en: The tower silhouette is copied onto the chessboard.
branches.cn: 塔楼的轮廓被复制到了棋盘上。

branches.en: Later castles become grand homes as much as forts.
branches.cn: 后来的城堡既是堡垒，也成为气派的宅邸。

branches.en: Both senses keep the tower as their shared outline.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以塔楼作为共同轮廓。

branches.en: The sandcastle is a playful miniature of the same walls.
branches.cn: 沙堡就是同样城墙的玩闹缩微版。

intro.en: Castle forms a small family through the -an and -ated endings and a few compounds.
intro.cn: castle 通过 -an、-ated 词尾和少量复合词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base castrum, a fort, also appears in place names such as Chester and Lancaster.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 castrum（要塞）也出现在 Chester、Lancaster 等地名中。

items.example: The valley is full of castles.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷里到处是城堡。

items.example: The castellan met them at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 城堡主在大门迎接他们。

items.example: The house has a castellated roof.
items.exampleCN: 这所房子有城堡式的屋顶。

items.example: The tide washed the sandcastle away.
They stayed in a chateau in the Loire.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在卢瓦尔河畔的一座庄园里。

items.example: Castrum survives in many place names.
items.exampleCN: castrum 存留在许多地名中。

items.example: Castellum is the direct source of castle.
items.exampleCN: castellum 是 castle 的直接来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: castrum 指罗马军队的营寨。

definition_en: a small furry animal with whiskers and soft paws, often kept as a pet, or any animal of the same family
core_image: 柔软无声的脚掌和一双竖起的耳朵
scene: 深夜院子里传来轻轻的脚步。A grey cat slipped through the fence and disappeared.
sceneCN: 这里 cat 指「猫」（第 1 个义项：常见的小型家养动物）；句意是一只灰猫从篱笆缝里钻过去不见了。

collocations.phrase: let the cat out of the bag

senses.title: A small domestic feline
senses.definition: a small furry animal with soft paws and whiskers, kept as a pet or kept to catch mice
senses.definitionCN: 一种毛茸茸、脚掌柔软、有胡须的小动物，常被当作宠物或用来捕鼠
senses.example: The cat slept on the warm windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 猫在温暖的窗台上睡着了。
senses.why: The core image of soft paws and pointed ears belongs to the everyday house cat.
senses.whyCN: 柔软脚掌与尖耳朵这一核心意象，正属于日常所见家猫。

senses.title: Any member of the feline family
senses.definition: any wild or domestic animal of the family that includes lions, tigers and cats
senses.definitionCN: 包括狮、虎和家猫在内的猫科中的任何野生或家养动物
senses.example: The lion is a big cat with a loud roar.
senses.exampleCN: 狮子是一种会大声吼叫的大型猫科动物。
senses.why: Biologists group the house cat with its large wild relatives, so cat widens to the whole family.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家把家猫与其大型野生近亲归为一类，于是 cat 扩展为整个猫科。

intro.en: Cat is an old English word whose deeper origin is uncertain, though it is usually traced through Late Latin cattus.
intro.cn: cat 是古英语旧词，更深来源不确定，通常认为经由晚期拉丁语 cattus 传来。

items.en: Cattus is the first well-recorded form, probably borrowed from an African or Semitic language.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cattus 是较早的可靠记录形式，可能借自非洲或闪米特语。

items.en: Catt appears in Old English for the domestic animal, with separate words for male and female.
items.cn: 古英语 catt 指家猫，公猫与母猫另有说法。

items.en: Cat replaces the older plural forms and becomes the general word.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，cat 取代旧的复数形式，成为通称。

items.en: The word enters idioms such as let the cat out of the bag.
items.cn: 该词进入「let the cat out of the bag」等习语。

items.en: Cat extends to big cats and to compounds such as cat food and tomcat.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cat 扩展到大型猫科，并构成 cat food、tomcat 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows English formations on cat, and the meaning group lists felines and their young.
note.cn: 形近组沿英语中由 cat 构成的词展开，近义组列出猫科动物及幼崽。

entries.definition: saying unkind things about others
moving or looking like a cat
the quality of being spiteful
a young cat
relating to cats, or a cat-like animal
entries.definitionCN: 与猫有关的，或猫一样的动物

entries.definition: a male cat

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin source, the idioms and the small family of cat compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语来源、常见习语以及 cat 的小词族。

normal.en: Cat, kitten and tomcat split the animal by age and sex, all inside one short family.
normal.cn: cat、kitten、tomcat 按年龄和性别划分这种动物，都在一个短短的词族里。

normal.en: Let the cat out of the bag pictures a secret escaping like an animal from a sack.
normal.cn: 「let the cat out of the bag」把秘密想象成从袋子里跑出来的动物。

normal.en: Rain cats and dogs is pure idiom, with no link to the animal's habits.
normal.cn: rain cats and dogs 纯属习语，与猫狗的真实习性无关。

normal.en: Big cat covers lions and tigers, showing how one word widens to a whole family.
normal.cn: big cat 覆盖狮子和老虎，说明一个词如何扩展到整个科。

normal.en: The plural cats is regular, so the noun needs only one extra letter.
normal.cn: 复数 cats 变化规则，名词只多一个字母。

abstract.en: Picture a cat landing without a sound on a narrow wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫无声地落在窄墙上。

abstract.en: Picture green eyes opening in a dark garden.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一双绿眼睛睁开。

abstract.en: Picture a kitten tangled in a ball of wool.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小猫缠在毛线球里。

examples.en: The cat followed me all the way home.
examples.cn: 那只猫一路跟着我回家。

examples.en: She feeds every stray cat in the street.
examples.cn: 她喂街上每一只流浪猫。

examples.en: A tiger is a big cat.
examples.cn: 老虎是一种大型猫科动物。

dict_mnemonic.text: cat 只有三个字母，读音短促像猫叫：记住这个短音，就记住了这种轻声走路的动物。

root: 古英语 catt，通常认为经晚期拉丁语 cattus 传来，更深来源不确定，可能与非洲或闪米特语有关。

sensesIntro.en: The small domestic animal gives the everyday sense, and biology widens the same name to lions and tigers.
sensesIntro.cn: 家养的小动物给出日常义，生物学又把同一个名称扩展到狮虎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft paws, whiskers and pointed ears.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的脚掌、胡须与尖耳朵。

branches.en: The house pet keeps the soft paws and the quiet walk.
branches.cn: 家猫保留了软脚掌和无声的步伐。

branches.en: Biology extends the name to lions, tigers and leopards.
branches.cn: 生物学把这个名称扩展到狮、虎和豹。

branches.en: Farm cats earn their place by catching mice.
branches.cn: 农场的猫靠捕鼠赢得自己的位置。

branches.en: Both share the same body plan, only the size differs.
branches.cn: 两者身体结构相同，只是大小不同。

branches.en: Idioms turn the cat into a figure of secrets and heavy rain.
branches.cn: 习语把猫变成秘密与大雨的形象。

intro.en: Cat forms a small family with -y, -like and -ness, plus a few familiar compounds.
intro.cn: cat 通过 -y、-like、-ness 以及几个常见复合词形成小词族。

latinIntro.en: The recorded Latin form is cattus, itself probably borrowed from outside the Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的拉丁语形式是 cattus，它本身很可能借自拉丁语族之外。

items.example: Two cats sat on the wall.
Her catty remark spoiled the evening.
items.exampleCN: 她那句刻薄话毁了整个晚上。

items.example: There was real cattiness in the office.
items.exampleCN: 办公室里确有刻薄之风。

items.example: Cattus is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: cattus 是较早的记录形式。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cattus 传遍了中世纪的欧洲。

definition_zh: 目录；目录册；一系列；编入目录
definition_en: a book or list that names things in order, especially goods or library holdings, or to enter items into such a list
core_image: 一页页排好的条目，像账簿一样整齐
scene: 拍卖行整理本季的拍品。The auction house printed a thick catalogue of paintings.
sceneCN: 这里 catalogue 指「目录册」（第 1 个义项：装订成册的条目清单）；句意是拍卖行印了一本厚厚的画作目录。

senses.title: A book listing items
senses.definition: a printed book or document that lists goods, works of art or books in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序列出商品、艺术品或书籍的印刷册子或文件
senses.example: The gallery sent me its new catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊给我寄来了新目录。
senses.why: The Greek list word was first spoken, then written, and finally bound as a book.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的清单词先从口头念出，再写下来，最后装订成册。

senses.title: A long series of events
senses.definition: a continuous series of things, especially unpleasant ones, that seem to be counted off
senses.definitionCN: 连续发生的一串事情，尤指像是被逐项数出的不快之事
senses.example: The year was a catalogue of mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年是一连串错误的集合。
senses.why: If a catalogue counts items, then a year full of faults can itself be read as a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 既然目录是逐项清点，那么满是过失的一年本身也能读成一份目录。

senses.title: To enter items in a list
senses.definition: to record objects or works in an ordered list, often with numbers and descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 把物品或作品记入有序清单，常附编号与说明
senses.example: They catalogued the letters before storing them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们先把信件编目，然后才归档。
senses.why: To catalogue is to do the counting work that produces a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 编目就是做那份清点工作，从而产生一份目录。

intro.en: Catalogue keeps the French spelling of the Greek list word, and its -ue ending still marks the British form today.
intro.cn: catalogue 保留了希腊语清单词的法语拼写，结尾的 -ue 至今是英式拼写的标志。

items.en: Katalogos meant a list or register, from kata and legein, to say or count.
items.cn: 希腊语 katalogos 意为清单或名录，由 kata 与 legein（说、点数）构成。

items.en: Catalogus carried the word into the written culture of the Roman world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 把该词带入罗马世界的书写文化。

items.en: Catalogue gave English the -ue spelling that British usage still prefers.
items.cn: 法语 catalogue 给英语留下了英式用法偏爱的 -ue 拼写。

items.en: Catalogue is recorded as a list of names or books arranged for reference.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语中，catalogue 已有按序排列名称或书籍的记录。

items.en: Art dealers and libraries make the printed catalogue a standard tool.
items.cn: 十九世纪艺术品商人与图书馆把印刷目录变成标准工具。

items.en: The phrase a catalogue of disasters fixes the figurative series sense.
items.cn: 短语 a catalogue of disasters 固定了比喻性的「一连串」义。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the -ue spelling and its derivatives, and the meaning group gives other records.
note.cn: 形近组留在 -ue 拼写及其派生词内，近义组给出其他记录形式。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
a person who compiles a catalogue
the process of listing items
an official list kept as a record
a detailed list of goods in stock
a book listing names, addresses or services
entries.definitionCN: 列出名称、地址或服务的册子

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the French -ue ending, the auction phrases and the disaster idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用法语式 -ue 词尾、拍卖场搭配以及灾难习语。

normal.en: The -ue ending is the British mark, just as in colour and theatre.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ue 是英式标志，就像 colour 与 theatre 的拼写。

normal.en: Catalogue and dialogue share the Greek root legein, to speak or count.
normal.cn: catalogue 与 dialogue 共享希腊语词根 legein（说或点数）。

normal.en: Auction catalogue and exhibition catalogue fix the printed-book sense.
normal.cn: auction catalogue 与 exhibition catalogue 固定了印刷册子义。

normal.en: A catalogue of disasters is a whole year of trouble read aloud.
normal.cn: a catalogue of disasters 就是把一整年的麻烦逐条念出来。

normal.en: Catalogue numbers give each listed work a small address of its own.
normal.cn: 目录编号给每件列出的作品一个小地址。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with gilt numbers down the spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书，书脊上印着烫金编号。

abstract.en: Picture an auctioneer tapping a page of listed paintings.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖师敲着写满画作的那一页。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of boxes, each labelled with a neat number.
abstract.cn: 想象一整排箱子，每只都标着整齐的编号。

examples.en: The catalogue lists every piece in the show.
examples.cn: 目录列出了展览中的每件作品。

examples.en: She found the price in the auction catalogue.
examples.cn: 她在拍卖目录里找到了价格。

examples.en: The collection was catalogued over ten years.
examples.cn: 这批藏品用了十年时间编目。

dict_mnemonic.text: catalogue 里的 log 是记录：把展品一件件记进本子，就成了一本目录册。

root: 与 catalog 同源，出自希腊语 katalogos（清单），经拉丁语 catalogus 与法语 catalogue 进入英语，-ue 为法式拼写残留。

sensesIntro.en: A spoken counting-off becomes a printed book, then a year of misfortunes, while the verb names the counting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 口头的逐项点数变成印刷册子，再变成一年的不幸，而动词则指点数这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered entries standing in neat rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：编了号、排成整齐行列的条目。

branches.en: The written list is bound and sold as a catalogue.
branches.cn: 写下的清单被装订起来，作为目录册出售。

branches.en: A run of bad events is counted off like entries.
branches.cn: 一连串坏事像条目一样被逐项数出。

branches.en: The verb performs the counting that fills the book.
branches.cn: 动词义执行填入册子的清点工作。

branches.en: Book and action are two sides of the same ordered record.
branches.cn: 册子与动作是同一份有序记录的两面。

branches.en: Both senses rely on the feeling of a long, orderly series.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「长而有序的一串」这种感觉。

intro.en: Catalogue forms -er and -ing nouns and keeps the French -ue in every British spelling.
intro.cn: catalogue 构成 -er 与 -ing 名词，英式拼写始终保留法语式 -ue。

latinIntro.en: Latin catalogus kept the Greek list word, which French later reshaped as catalogue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 保留了希腊语清单词，法语后来把它改写成 catalogue。

items.example: The cataloguer noted a missing page.
items.exampleCN: 编目员注意到缺了一页。

items.meaning: the same word in American English

items.exampleCN: catalogus 见于中世纪图书馆。

latinEntries.example: Catalogus is the Latin bridge to English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: catalogus 是通向英语的拉丁语桥梁。

definition_zh: 抓住；接住；赶上；染上；听懂
definition_en: to take hold of something moving, to reach a bus or train in time, to get an illness, or to hear and understand something
core_image: 伸手一扑，把正在动的东西按在手里
scene: 球场上队友把球高高抛起。He jumped and caught the ball with one hand.
sceneCN: 这里 catch 指「接住」（第 1 个义项：用手抓住运动中的东西）；句意是他跳起来，单手接住了球。

pos.zh: 抓住；接住；赶上；染上；听懂

senses.title: To take hold of something moving
senses.definition: to stop and hold a moving object with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手拦住并握住运动中的物体
senses.example: She caught the keys he threw her.
senses.exampleCN: 她接住了他扔来的钥匙。
senses.why: The core image is a hand closing on something in flight, and that is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只手合拢在飞行中的东西上，这也是最古老的义项。

senses.title: To reach a bus or train in time
senses.definition: to arrive early enough to get on a bus, train, plane or boat
senses.definitionCN: 到得够早，能登上公交、火车、飞机或船
senses.example: We ran and caught the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑着赶上了末班车。
senses.why: A departing vehicle is a moving target, so boarding it in time is catching it.
senses.whyCN: 开走的车就是一个移动目标，及时登上它也就是「抓住」它。

senses.title: To get an illness
senses.definition: to become infected with a disease or pick up an illness from others
senses.definitionCN: 被疾病感染，或从他人那里染上病
senses.example: He caught a cold after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行之后他感冒了。
senses.why: An illness is pictured as something passing by that the body seizes.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被想象成从身边经过、被身体抓住的东西。

senses.title: To hear and understand
senses.definition: to manage to hear words or understand a joke or meaning
senses.definitionCN: 设法听清话语，或理解笑话与含义
senses.example: I did not catch what she said.
senses.exampleCN: 我没听清她说什么。
senses.why: Understanding is pictured as grabbing hold of words before they fly away.
senses.whyCN: 理解被想象成在话语飞走之前把它抓住。

intro.en: Catch came through northern French from a Latin verb meaning to try to seize, and its spelling kept the French sound.
intro.cn: catch 经法国北部方言上溯到拉丁语中意为试图抓取的动词，拼写保留了法语读音。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and captare meant to keep trying to seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取，captare 意为反复试图抓取。

items.en: Cachier meant to chase or hunt, a northern French form of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古北法语 cachier 意为追捕，是拉丁语动词的北部方言形式。

items.en: Cacchen appears in the thirteenth century for chasing and seizing.
items.cn: 中古英语 cacchen 在十三世纪已指追逐与抓取。

items.en: The word extends to catching a train, catching cold and catching meaning.
items.cn: 此后词义扩展到赶车、受凉和听懂意思。

items.en: Modern idioms add catch fire, catch sight of and catch up with.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上着火、瞥见和追上等习语。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the English family of catch, while the meaning group lists other verbs for seizing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 catch 的英语词族展开，近义组列出其他表示抓取的动词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that catches
able to spread from person to person
entries.definitionCN: 能在人与人之间传染的

entries.definition: easy to remember and repeat
to take hold of something suddenly and firmly
to take something quickly with the hand
to take a person or animal prisoner

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie catch to its Latin seize root, to the irregular past caught and to common idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 catch 与拉丁语抓取词根、不规则过去式 caught 以及常见习语连起来。

normal.en: Catch and capture share the Latin root cap, to take, which explains why both mean seizing.
normal.cn: catch 与 capture 共享拉丁语词根 cap（拿取），这解释了为什么两者都表示抓。

normal.en: The past tense is caught, rhyming with taught and bought, all old irregular forms.
normal.cn: 过去式是 caught，与 taught、bought 押韵，都是古老的不规则形式。

normal.en: Catch a cold pictures the illness as a passing object you grab.
normal.cn: catch a cold 把疾病想象成一个路过、被你抓住的东西。

normal.en: Catch a train keeps the same move: you reach the departing vehicle in time.
normal.cn: catch a train 保留同一动作：你及时够到了正在离开的车。

normal.en: Catchy music is music that catches in your head and will not leave.
normal.cn: catchy 的音乐就是抓住你脑子、赶不走的音乐。

abstract.en: Picture a hand snapping shut around a thrown ball.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手啪地合拢，扣住飞来的球。

abstract.en: Picture a runner sliding through closing train doors.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者从正在合拢的车门间挤进去。

abstract.en: Picture a word flying past and being snatched out of the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从耳边飞过，被凌空抓下。

examples.en: Can you catch the ball with your left hand?
examples.cn: 你能用左手接住球吗？

examples.en: I need to catch the early train tomorrow.
examples.cn: 我明天得赶早班火车。

examples.en: She caught a cold during the trip.
examples.cn: 她在旅途中感冒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: catch 短促有力，像手掌「咔」一下合上：抓住球、抓住车、抓住病、抓住话里的意思。

root: 源自古北法语 cachier（追捕），上溯拉丁语 captare（反复试图抓取），是 capere（拿取）的反复形式。

sensesIntro.en: One snatching gesture extends to vehicles, illnesses and words, because all of them are things that pass and can be seized.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个抓取动作扩展到车、病和话，因为它们都是经过身边、可以被抓住的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on something in motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在运动中的东西上。

branches.en: The literal hand closes on a ball, a rope or a key.
branches.cn: 字面义是手合拢在球、绳或钥匙上。

branches.en: A departing vehicle is caught by arriving in time.
branches.cn: 开走的车靠及时赶到而被「抓住」。

branches.en: An illness is caught as it passes through the air.
branches.cn: 疾病像从空气里经过时被抓住。

branches.en: Meaning is caught when the words are held long enough to be understood.
branches.cn: 话语被握住足够久、听明白了，意思就被抓住。

branches.en: Both depend on speed and timing rather than strength.
branches.cn: 两者都取决于速度和时机，而非力量。

intro.en: Catch forms agent and adjective nouns with -er, -ing and -y, and keeps an irregular past.
intro.cn: catch 用 -er、-ing、-y 构成名词与形容词，并保留不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base capere, to take, is the same root behind capture, captive and accept.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 capere（拿取）也是 capture、captive 与 accept 的词根。

items.example: She catches every cold going round.
items.exampleCN: 流行什么感冒她都染上。

items.example: They caught the thief at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他们在大门口抓住了小偷。

items.meaning: spreading, or in the act of seizing
items.meaningCN: 有传染性的，或正在抓取

items.example: The catcher signalled for a fast ball.
The song has a catchy chorus.
Captare is the source of catch.
items.exampleCN: captare 是 catch 的来源。
capere 也是 capture 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Capere is the base of many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 是许多英语词的词基。
captare 传入了法国北部方言。

definition_en: a group of people or things that share a particular quality, or a basic class in philosophy and logic
core_image: 把一大堆东西分进贴着标签的格子
scene: 评委把参赛作品分成几组。Each entry was placed in a different category.
sceneCN: 这里 category 指「类别」（第 1 个义项：按共同特点划分的一组）；句意是每件参赛作品都被归入不同的类别。

senses.title: A class of similar things
senses.definition: a group of people or things that share a common feature and are treated together
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同特点、被放在一起处理的一组人或物
senses.example: These films belong to the same category.
senses.exampleCN: 这些影片属于同一类别。
senses.why: The Greek word was a public statement about what something is, and naming a class is exactly that kind of statement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词是对某物是什么的公开断言，而给一个类别命名正是这种断言。

senses.title: A basic class in logic
senses.definition: one of the most general classes used to analyse reality, such as quantity, quality or relation
senses.definitionCN: 用于分析现实的最普遍类别，如数量、性质或关系
senses.example: Kant listed twelve categories of understanding.
senses.exampleCN: 康德列出了十二个知性范畴。
senses.why: Philosophy takes the everyday class word and raises it to the widest possible divisions of thought.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常的类别词提升为思维中最宽泛的划分。

intro.en: Category began as a Greek word for a public accusation, then became the logical term for what can be stated of a thing.
intro.cn: category 最初是希腊语中公开指控的说法，后来成为逻辑学中「关于某物能说什么」的术语。

items.en: Agora was the public assembly, and agoreuein meant to speak in public.
items.cn: 希腊语 agora 指公民大会，agoreuein 意为当众发言。

items.en: Kategoria meant an accusation, a statement made publicly against someone.
items.cn: kategoria 意为指控，即当众针对某人作出的陈述。

items.en: Aristotle used the word for the basic ways something can be predicated, such as quantity or relation.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用该词指述说某物的基本方式，如数量或关系。

items.en: Categoria was borrowed into Latin as a technical term of logic.
items.cn: categoria 作为逻辑学术语被借入拉丁语。

items.en: French categorie carried the logical term into ordinary classification.
items.cn: 法语 categorie 把这个逻辑术语带入日常分类。

items.en: Modern English uses category for any practical grouping, from age groups to product types.
items.cn: 现代英语用 category 指任何实用分组，从年龄组到产品类型。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the classify family, while the meaning group gives other grouping words.
note.cn: 形近组沿分类词族展开，近义组给出其他表示分组的词。

entries.definition: to put things into classes
the act of sorting into classes
stated without conditions or doubt
entries.definitionCN: 无条件、毫不含糊地陈述的

entries.definition: a group of things of the same kind
a kind or sort of person or thing
a set of people or things placed together
entries.definitionCN: 放在一起的一组人或物

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the public-speech root, the -ize and -ical family and the everyday grouping phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「当众发言」词根、-ize 与 -ical 词族以及日常分组搭配。

normal.en: Category and categorize differ by the -ize ending, which turns the class into an action.
normal.cn: category 与 categorize 只差 -ize 词尾，后者把类别变成动作。

normal.en: The Greek root agora, a public square, also appears in agoraphobia, fear of open spaces.
normal.cn: 希腊语词根 agora（公共广场）也出现在 agoraphobia（广场恐惧）里。

normal.en: Age category and product category show the word doing practical sorting work.
normal.cn: age category 与 product category 展示这个词的实际分组功能。

normal.en: Categorical answers leave no room for doubt, as if the class were fixed for ever.
normal.cn: categorical 的回答不留怀疑余地，仿佛类别已经永久定死。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies, so one category becomes many categories.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变成 ies，一个 category 变成许多 categories。

abstract.en: Picture a market square where a speaker names each item aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象集市广场上有人高声给每样东西归类。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of labelled drawers, each holding one kind of thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一面贴着标签的抽屉墙，每格只放一类东西。

abstract.en: Picture a judge sorting cards into neat piles on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判在桌上把卡片分成整齐的几堆。

examples.en: The prize has a separate category for young writers.
examples.cn: 该奖项为年轻作者单设一个类别。

examples.en: Books in this category sell quickly.
examples.cn: 这一类别的书卖得很快。

examples.en: Please categorize the files by date.
examples.cn: 请按日期把文件分类。

dict_mnemonic.text: category 里有 cate 加 gory：想象把东西按标签排成一排排格子，每一格就是一个类别。

root: 源自希腊语 kategoria（公开指控、断言），由 kata（针对）与 agoreuein（当众发言）构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A public statement about what something is becomes a logical class, then any practical grouping of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 关于某物是什么的公开断言变成逻辑类别，再变成任何实用的分组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled slot into which similar things are sorted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个贴着标签、用来归放同类物的格子。

branches.en: Philosophy keeps the widest classes of predication.
branches.cn: 哲学保留了最宽泛的述谓类别。

branches.en: Everyday use narrows the class to any group sharing a feature.
branches.cn: 日常用法把类别收窄为任何共享某一特点的组。

branches.en: Age category and product category apply the grouping to people and goods.
branches.cn: 年龄组与产品类别把分组用到人和货物上。

branches.en: Both senses answer the question of what kind of thing something is.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在回答「这属于哪一种东西」。

branches.en: The logical sense stays technical and mostly appears in philosophy.
branches.cn: 逻辑义偏技术性，多出现在哲学文本中。

intro.en: Category builds verbs and nouns with -ize and -ization, and an adjective with -ical.
intro.cn: category 用 -ize、-ization 构成动词与名词，用 -ical 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin categoria preserved the Greek term of logic, which French later passed to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 categoria 保留了希腊语逻辑术语，法语后来把它传给英语。

items.exampleCN: kategoria 经亚里士多德进入逻辑学。
agora 藏在 kategoria 之中。

latinEntries.example: Categoria passed from Greek into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: categoria 从希腊语进入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 原因；起因；事业；导致；引起
definition_en: the person or thing that makes something happen, a principle that people support, or to make something happen
core_image: 推倒第一块骨牌的那只手
scene: 调查人员围着一台烧坏的机器。A loose wire was the cause of the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 cause 指「原因」（第 1 个义项：使事情发生的事物）；句意是一根松动的电线是起火的起因。

senses.title: The reason something happens
senses.definition: the person, thing or event that makes another thing happen
senses.definitionCN: 使另一件事发生的人、物或事件
senses.example: The police are still looking for the cause of the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 警方仍在查找撞车的原因。
senses.why: The Latin word first named a legal case, then the reason behind any effect.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源词先指法律案件，后指任何结果背后的理由。

senses.title: A principle people support
senses.definition: an aim or principle that a group works for and defends
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体为之努力并捍卫的目标或原则
senses.example: She gave her life to the cause of education.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一生献给了教育事业。
senses.why: A cause worth arguing for in court becomes a cause worth working for in public life.
senses.whyCN: 值得在法庭上力争的事由，变成了值得在公共生活中奋斗的事业。

senses.title: To make something happen
senses.definition: to be the reason that an event, problem or change occurs
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事件、问题或变化发生的原因
senses.example: Heavy rain caused the river to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨使河水上涨。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the noun around: to be the cause is to cause.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词反过来用：成为原因，就是去导致。

intro.en: Cause comes from a Latin word for a legal case, which widened to mean a reason and then a principle.
intro.cn: cause 来自拉丁语中表示法律案件的词，后来扩展为理由，再扩展为事业。

items.en: Causa meant a lawsuit, a plea, and also the reason behind something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 causa 指诉讼、申辩，也指某事背后的理由。

items.en: Cause kept both the legal and the explanatory senses in medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 cause 在中世纪同时保留法律义与解释义。

items.en: English cause first names a reason or motive, and the legal sense fades.
items.cn: 英语 cause 最初指理由或动机，法律义逐渐淡化。

items.en: The word extends to a principle defended in public, such as a political cause.
items.cn: 词义扩展到公共生活中所捍卫的原则，如政治事业。

items.en: Cause and effect becomes the standard phrase for the relation between events.
items.cn: cause and effect 成为表示事件关系的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the causal family, and the meaning group lists other words for reasons and sources.
note.cn: 形近组沿因果词族展开，近义组列出其他表示理由与来源的词。

entries.definition: relating to cause and effect
the relation between cause and result
entries.definitionCN: 原因与结果之间的关系

entries.definition: for the reason that
a fact that explains why something happens
entries.definitionCN: 解释某事为何发生的事实

entries.definition: the place or thing something comes from
entries.definitionCN: 某物来自的地方或事物

entries.definition: a reason for acting in a certain way
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行动的理由

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the legal origin, the causal family and the fixed contrast with effect.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用法律来源、因果词族以及与 effect 的固定对照。

normal.en: Cause and case both come from Latin causa, which first meant a lawsuit.
normal.cn: cause 与 case 都出自拉丁语 causa，最初指诉讼。

normal.en: Cause and effect always travel as a pair: the reason and the result.
normal.cn: cause 与 effect 总是成对出现：原因与结果。

normal.en: Because literally means by cause, which is why it answers the question why.
normal.cn: because 字面上是「由原因」，所以它回答为什么。

normal.en: Causal and causality keep the adjective and noun forms of the same idea.
normal.cn: causal 与 causality 保留了同一概念的形容词与名词形式。

normal.en: To cause something is simply to be its cause, with no change of meaning.
normal.cn: to cause 某物就是成为它的 cause，词义没有改变。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing the first domino in a long row.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手推倒长排骨牌的第一块。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd marching behind a single banner.
abstract.cn: 想象人群跟在同一面旗帜后面前进。

abstract.en: Picture a broken wire still smoking on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象地上那根还在冒烟的断线。

examples.en: Nobody knows the cause of the illness.
examples.cn: 没人知道这种病的原因。

examples.en: The storm caused serious damage.
examples.cn: 暴风雨造成了严重破坏。

examples.en: She has long supported the cause of clean water.
examples.cn: 她长期支持清洁用水这项事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: cause 与 because 是一家：because 就是「由 cause 而来」，说出原因，也就说出了 cause。

root: 源自拉丁语 causa（诉讼、理由），经古法语 cause 进入英语，由法律案件扩展为原因与事业。

sensesIntro.en: A legal case becomes a reason, a reason becomes a principle worth defending, and the verb makes the reason act.
sensesIntro.cn: 法律案件变成理由，理由变成值得捍卫的事业，动词则让这个理由发挥作用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first push that sets everything else moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：最初那一下推动，让后面的一切动起来。

branches.en: The reason sense answers the plain question why.
branches.cn: 原因义回答最朴素的「为什么」。

branches.en: A principle argued for becomes a cause people serve.
branches.cn: 被力争的原则变成了人们献身的事业。

branches.en: The verb makes the reason into an action.
branches.cn: 动词义把理由变成动作。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in whether the cause is named or applied.
branches.cn: 名词与动词只差在原因是被告知还是被施行。

branches.en: Both senses involve something worth standing behind.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及值得站在其后支持的东西。

intro.en: Cause builds adjectives and nouns with -al and -ality, and hides inside because.
intro.cn: cause 用 -al 与 -ality 构成形容词和名词，还藏在 because 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin causa is also the source of accuse and excuse, both built on the legal sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 causa 也是 accuse 与 excuse 的来源，两者都建立在法律义上。

items.meaning: the relation of cause to effect
items.exampleCN: 这项研究质疑因果关系。

items.example: We stayed because of the rain.
Causa is the source of cause.
items.exampleCN: causa 是 cause 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: causa 也是 accuse 的来源。

definition_en: to stop happening or doing something, or to come to an end
core_image: 正在转动的轮子被人按住，慢慢停住
scene: 机器发出怪响，工人按下开关。The noise ceased as soon as the power was cut.
sceneCN: 这里 cease 指「停止」（第 1 个义项：声音不再继续）；句意是电源一断，噪音立刻停止了。

senses.title: To stop doing or happening
senses.definition: to bring or come to an end, especially of an activity or a sound
senses.definitionCN: 使活动或声音结束，或自身结束
senses.example: The rain ceased at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 雨在半夜停了。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to hold back or delay, and holding something back ends its motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是拦住或拖延，而把某物拦住就是终止它的运动。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.definition: to come to an end as a thing that exists, often used of companies or species
senses.definitionCN: 作为存在物走到尽头，常用于公司或物种
senses.example: The old factory ceased to exist in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老厂在九十年代就不存在了。
senses.why: When an activity stops for ever, the thing that carried it out also stops existing.
senses.whyCN: 当一项活动永久停止，从事这项活动的事物也就不再存在。

intro.en: Cease comes from a Latin verb meaning to delay or hold back, which passed through French into English.
intro.cn: cease 来自一个意为拖延或拦住的拉丁语动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Cessare meant to be slow, to delay or to leave off an activity.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cessare 意为迟缓、拖延或停止某项活动。

items.en: Cesser carried the sense of stopping and yielding into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 cesser 把停止与让出的含义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: Cesen appears in the fourteenth century for leaving off an action.
items.cn: 中古英语 cesen 在十四世纪已指停止某项行动。

items.en: Legal and military phrases such as cease and desist and cease fire become fixed.
items.cn: 停止并终止、停火等法律与军事说法逐渐固定。

items.en: Cease to exist extends the word from actions to the ending of things themselves.
items.cn: cease to exist 把该词从动作扩展到事物本身的终结。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cessation family, while the meaning group lists other verbs for ending.
note.cn: 形近组沿停止词族展开，近义组列出其他表示结束的动词。

entries.definition: a stopping of an activity
never stopping
without a pause
to end movement or action
to stop suddenly, especially marching
to come or bring to a finish

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie cease to cessation, to the legal phrase and to the picture of a stopped wheel.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cease 与 cessation、法律短语以及停住的轮子连起来。

normal.en: Cease and cessation share one root, so ending an action and the end itself sit side by side.
normal.cn: cease 与 cessation 同根，停止动作与停止状态并排而立。

normal.en: Cease fire is the shortest way to remember the military use.
normal.cn: cease fire 是记住军事用法最短的方式。

normal.en: Cease to exist puts the word before a verb, a pattern shared with fail to and happen to.
normal.cn: cease to exist 把词放在动词前，与 fail to、happen to 同型。

normal.en: Ceaseless keeps the word but adds -less, so it means without any cease.
normal.cn: ceaseless 保留词干再加 -less，意思就是毫无停止。

normal.en: The spelling has ea but the sound is a long ee, as in peace and please.
normal.cn: 拼写是 ea，读音却是长音 ee，如同 peace 与 please。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy wheel slowing until it stands still.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的轮子慢下来，最后静止。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed on a switch and a sudden silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在开关上，四周忽然安静。

abstract.en: Picture a factory gate rusting shut for the last time.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂大门最后一次生锈地合上。

examples.en: The rain finally ceased in the afternoon.
examples.cn: 雨终于在下午停了。

examples.en: Both sides agreed to cease fire at dawn.
examples.cn: 双方同意在黎明停火。

examples.en: That company ceased to exist years ago.
examples.cn: 那家公司多年前就不存在了。

dict_mnemonic.text: cease 读音像「息死」：气息一停，动作也就停了。

root: 源自拉丁语 cessare（迟缓、停止），经古法语 cesser 进入英语；cessation 与之同根。

sensesIntro.en: Holding something back stops an action, and a permanent stop removes the thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某物拦住会让动作停下，而永久的停止则让事物本身消失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a turning wheel brought to rest by a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：转动的轮子被一只手按住停下。

branches.en: A sound or activity stops and the word names the moment.
branches.cn: 声音或活动停下，这个词就命名那个时刻。

branches.en: A permanent stop extends to the ending of the thing itself.
branches.cn: 永久停止扩展到事物本身的终结。

branches.en: Cease fire keeps the sense in military commands.
branches.cn: cease fire 把该义保留在军事口令里。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of no further movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「不再有后续运动」的意思。

branches.en: Cease to exist is the formal way to say a thing is gone.
branches.cn: cease to exist 是「事物已消失」的正式说法。

intro.en: Cease forms its family with -less and -ation, and keeps a fixed legal phrase.
intro.cn: cease 用 -less 与 -ation 构成词族，并保留一条固定法律短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin cessare, to delay, also underlies cessation and the legal word cessor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cessare（拖延）也是 cessation 与法律词 cessor 的词根。

items.example: The ceasing of the rain surprised us.
A cessation of fighting was agreed.

items.exampleCN: 无休止的噪音让所有人都累了。

items.example: Cessare is the source of cease.
items.exampleCN: cessare 是 cease 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Cessare passed through French as cesser.

definition_zh: 天花板；顶棚；上限；云底高度
definition_en: the inner surface at the top of a room, or the highest level that something is allowed to reach
core_image: 头顶上那层封住房间的平面
scene: 老房子的房间很高。A single lamp hung from the high ceiling.
sceneCN: 这里 ceiling 指「天花板」（第 1 个义项：房间顶部的内表面）；句意是一盏灯从高高的天花板上垂下来。

senses.title: The top surface of a room
senses.definition: the inside surface that covers the top of a room
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖房间顶部的内表面
senses.example: The ceiling is painted white.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板刷成了白色。
senses.why: The old verb meant to line or panel a room, and the panel above your head became the ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 旧动词意为给房间装衬板，头顶上那层衬板就成了天花板。

senses.title: The highest allowed level
senses.definition: the greatest amount or level that is officially allowed or possible
senses.definitionCN: 官方允许或可能达到的最大数量或水平
senses.example: The government set a ceiling on rents.
senses.exampleCN: 政府给租金设了上限。
senses.why: A ceiling is a fixed surface you cannot rise above, so any hard limit borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 天花板是一层无法越过的固定平面，于是任何硬性限制都借用了这个画面。

senses.title: The height of the cloud base
senses.definition: the height above the ground at which the lowest clouds begin, used in flying
senses.definitionCN: 最低云层离地面的高度，用于飞行
senses.example: The pilot reported a low ceiling over the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员报告海岸上空云底很低。
senses.why: To a pilot the cloud base is literally a roof over the aircraft, so the room word fits.
senses.whyCN: 对飞行员来说，云底字面上就是飞机头顶的屋顶，房间用词正好合用。

intro.en: Ceiling comes from an old verb meaning to line or hide, not from any word for sky.
intro.cn: ceiling 来自一个意为衬里或遮盖的旧动词，与表示天空的词无关。

items.en: Celare meant to hide or conceal, and its French descendant kept that sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celare 意为隐藏或遮盖，其法语后裔保留了这个意思。

items.en: Celer meant to conceal, and also to panel or line the inside of a room.
items.cn: 古法语 celer 意为遮盖，也指给房间内侧装衬板。

items.en: Celen names the panelling of walls and roofs, especially the upper lining of a room.
items.cn: 中古英语 celen 指给墙和屋顶装衬板，尤其是房间上部的衬层。

items.en: Ceiling settles as the noun for the inner roof of a room.
items.cn: 十六世纪 ceiling 固定为指房间内侧顶面的名词。

items.en: The word spreads to price ceilings, glass ceilings and the cloud base seen by pilots.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩展到价格上限、无形障碍以及飞行员所见的云底。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the old verb and its adjective, while the meaning group gives other upper limits.
note.cn: 形近组保留旧动词及其形容词，近义组给出其他上部或限度说法。

entries.definition: to fit a room with a ceiling
having a ceiling of a stated kind
the outer covering on top of a building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物顶部的外层覆盖

entries.definition: an upper limit placed on an amount
the greatest amount allowed

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the conceal root, the price phrases and the false link with sky.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用遮盖词根、价格搭配，以及与天空的错误联想。

normal.en: Ceiling and conceal share the Latin root celare, to hide, because a ceiling covers the room.
normal.cn: ceiling 与 conceal 共享拉丁语词根 celare（隐藏），因为天花板正是把房间盖住。

normal.en: The word has nothing to do with the Latin for sky, however tempting that link feels.
normal.cn: 尽管这层联想很诱人，这个词与拉丁语中表示天空的词毫无关系。

normal.en: Price ceiling and glass ceiling keep the limit sense in economics and at work.
normal.cn: price ceiling 与 glass ceiling 把上限义留在经济学与职场里。

normal.en: Hit the ceiling means explode with anger, as if your head struck the roof.
normal.cn: hit the ceiling 意思是暴怒，仿佛头撞到了屋顶。

normal.en: The plural ceilings simply adds an s to the -ing noun.
normal.cn: 复数 ceilings 只在 -ing 名词后加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a bare bulb swinging above a white plaster surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一只光灯泡在白色灰泥顶面下摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a pilot looking up at a flat grey layer of cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象飞行员抬头望见平坦的灰色云层。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on a rising graph line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把上升的曲线按住。

examples.en: The ceiling is too low for a tall bookshelf.
examples.cn: 天花板太低，放不下高书架。

examples.en: They put a ceiling on ticket prices.
examples.cn: 他们给票价设了上限。

examples.en: She has broken the glass ceiling in her company.
examples.cn: 她打破了公司里的无形晋升障碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: ceiling 可以想成「see 到顶」：抬头看见的那一层平面，就是天花板，也是上限。

root: 源自古法语 celer（遮盖、装衬板），上溯拉丁语 celare（隐藏），与表示天空的词无关。

sensesIntro.en: A lining that hides the roof beams becomes the room's upper surface, then any level you cannot rise above.
sensesIntro.cn: 遮住屋顶梁的衬层变成房间上部表面，再变成任何无法越过的水平线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat layer sealed over the space above your head.
core.cn: 核心意象：在头顶空间上封住的一层平面。

branches.en: The room surface keeps the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 房间顶面保留了最古老、最具体的义项。

branches.en: A limit borrows the picture of a surface you cannot pass.
branches.cn: 上限借用了无法穿过的平面这一画面。

branches.en: The cloud base becomes a roof for aircraft.
branches.cn: 云底成了飞机头顶的屋顶。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a top that stops upward movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「顶端阻止上升」的意思。

branches.en: Both are technical extensions of one plain physical image.
branches.cn: 两者都是同一个具体画面在技术领域的延伸。

intro.en: Ceiling keeps the old verb ceil and a participle-like adjective, plus compounds.
intro.cn: ceiling 保留了旧动词 ceil 和类似分词的形容词，并有若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb celare, to hide, underlies the word through French celer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 celare（隐藏）经法语 celer 构成这个词的底层来源。

items.meaning: the top surface of a room

items.example: The two rooms have high ceilings.
items.exampleCN: 两个房间的天花板都很高。

items.example: They ceiled the hall in oak.
items.exampleCN: 他们用橡木给大厅装了顶。

items.meaning: having a ceiling of a kind
items.exampleCN: 层高很低的房间让人感到温暖。

items.meaning: a fan fixed to the ceiling
items.meaningCN: 固定在天花板上的风扇

items.meaning: a lamp fixed to the ceiling
a legal upper limit on prices
items.example: The price ceiling hurt small shops.
items.exampleCN: 价格上限让小商店受了损。

items.example: Celare is the deep root of ceiling.
items.exampleCN: celare 是 ceiling 的深层词根。

latinEntries.example: Celare passed into French as celer.
latinEntries.exampleCN: celare 传入法语成为 celer。

definition_zh: 庆祝；庆贺；赞颂；主持（仪式）
definition_en: to do something enjoyable to mark a special occasion, to praise someone publicly, or to perform a religious ceremony
core_image: 人群聚在一起，为一件好事高声欢呼
scene: 球队赢下决赛的当晚，整条街都很热闹。The whole street came out to celebrate the victory.
sceneCN: 这里 celebrate 指「庆祝」（第 1 个义项：用热闹活动纪念喜事）；句意是整条街的人都出来庆祝这场胜利。

senses.title: To mark a happy occasion
senses.definition: to do something enjoyable in order to mark a special day or event
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念特别的日子或事件而做些令人愉快的事
senses.example: We celebrated her graduation with a dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们用一顿晚饭庆祝她毕业。
senses.why: A crowded gathering on a feast day is the oldest picture behind the word, and joy is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: 节日里人群聚集是这个词最古老的画面，而喜悦至今仍是它的中心。

senses.title: To praise someone publicly
senses.definition: to speak or write about someone's achievements with approval
senses.definitionCN: 带着赞许谈论或书写某人的成就
senses.example: The poem celebrates the courage of ordinary workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗赞颂普通工人的勇气。
senses.why: Public honour grows from public festivity: the crowd that gathers to rejoice can also gather to praise.
senses.whyCN: 公开的荣誉源自公开的欢庆：为高兴而聚集的人群，也能为赞美而聚集。

senses.title: To perform a religious ceremony
senses.definition: to lead or perform a formal religious rite such as Mass
senses.definitionCN: 主持弥撒等正式宗教仪式
senses.example: The priest celebrated Mass at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 神父在黎明主持了弥撒。
senses.why: Church ritual is a solemn gathering, so the verb for gathering to honour extends to conducting the rite.
senses.whyCN: 教会仪式是庄严的聚集，于是表示聚集致敬的动词也扩展到主持仪式。

intro.en: Celebrate comes from a Latin verb for honouring in a crowd, built on an adjective meaning crowded or famous.
intro.cn: celebrate 来自拉丁语中在人前致敬的动词，其词基是一个意为拥挤或著名的形容词。

items.en: Celeber meant crowded, busy or well known.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celeber 意为拥挤、繁忙或著名的。

items.en: Celebrare meant to gather in numbers and to honour someone publicly.
items.cn: celebrare 意为众人聚集，并公开向某人致敬。

items.en: English celebrate first appears in religious use, for performing a rite.
items.cn: 英语 celebrate 最早见于宗教用法，指举行仪式。

items.en: The word widens to feasting and merrymaking on special days.
items.cn: 词义扩展到在特别的日子里宴饮欢庆。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of praising a person or idea in art and writing.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上在艺术与文字中赞颂人物或观念的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the celebration family, while the meaning group lists other words for marking and honouring.
note.cn: 形近组沿庆祝词族展开，近义组列出其他表示纪念与致敬的词。

entries.definition: a party or event that marks something
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某事而办的聚会或活动

entries.definition: a famous person, or the state of being famous
expressing joy at a special event
entries.definitionCN: 为特别事件表达喜悦的

entries.definition: to remember and honour a person or event formally
entries.definitionCN: 正式纪念并致敬某人或某事

entries.definition: to feel or show great joy
entries.definitionCN: 感到或表现出极大喜悦

entries.definition: to show respect or praise publicly

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie celebrate to the crowded root, to celebration and to the fixed occasion phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 celebrate 与拥挤词根、celebration 以及固定场合搭配连起来。

normal.en: The Latin root celeber meant crowded, so to celebrate is to fill a place with people who care.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 celeber 意为拥挤，所以庆祝就是让在乎的人把地方填满。

normal.en: Celebration, celebrity and celebratory all keep the same -celebr- stem.
normal.cn: celebration、celebrity、celebratory 都保留同一个 -celebr- 词干。

normal.en: A celebrity is literally a much-celebrated person, one whose name is spoken everywhere.
normal.cn: celebrity 字面上就是被大家广泛称颂的人，名字到处被提起。

normal.en: Celebrate a birthday and celebrate success fix the joyful sense in daily life.
normal.cn: celebrate a birthday 与 celebrate success 把喜悦义固定在日常生活里。

normal.en: Celebrate Mass shows the older, religious sense surviving in church language.
normal.cn: celebrate Mass 显示较古老、宗教性的义项仍活在教会用语里。

abstract.en: Picture a street full of shouting people after a final whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象终场哨响后满街欢呼的人群。

abstract.en: Picture a raised glass and a table covered with dishes.
abstract.cn: 想象举起的酒杯和一桌菜肴。

abstract.en: Picture a choir singing under a high stone roof.
abstract.cn: 想象唱诗班在高大的石顶下歌唱。

examples.en: They celebrated their anniversary with a quiet trip.
examples.cn: 他们用一次安静的旅行庆祝结婚纪念日。

examples.en: The whole town celebrates the harvest each autumn.
examples.cn: 全镇每年秋天都庆祝丰收。

examples.en: The book celebrates the lives of ordinary people.
examples.cn: 这本书赞颂普通人的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: celebrate 里有 celebr：把它想成「塞勒布雷特」节的欢呼，人一聚齐，庆祝就开始了。

root: 源自拉丁语 celebrare（聚集致敬），词基 celeber 意为拥挤、著名，经中古英语进入宗教与日常用法。

sensesIntro.en: A crowded feast gives joyful celebration, public praise grows from the same crowd, and church ritual keeps the solemn side.
sensesIntro.cn: 人群聚集的宴饮给出欢庆，公开赞美从同一人群生长，教会仪式则保留庄严的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd gathered to honour one happy event.
core.cn: 核心意象：为一件喜事聚在一起的人群。

branches.en: The joyful feast is the sense most people use today.
branches.cn: 欢庆宴饮是今天最多人使用的义项。

branches.en: Public honour turns the crowd toward praise rather than party.
branches.cn: 公开荣誉把人群从聚会转向赞美。

branches.en: Religious ritual keeps the formal, gathered side of the word.
branches.cn: 宗教仪式保留了该词正式、聚集的一面。

branches.en: Both are ceremonies, one joyful and one solemn.
branches.cn: 两者都是仪式，一个欢快，一个庄严。

branches.en: Both put a person or event at the centre of public attention.
branches.cn: 两者都把人物或事件放在公众注意的中心。

intro.en: Celebrate builds nouns and adjectives with -ion, -ity and -ory, all on the same stem.
intro.cn: celebrate 用 -ion、-ity、-ory 在同一词干上构成名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base celeber, crowded or famous, also survives in celebrity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 celeber（拥挤或著名）也活在 celebrity 里。

items.meaning: he or she marks an event
items.exampleCN: 每个小小的胜利她都要庆祝。

items.example: The city is celebrating its birthday.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市正在庆祝建城纪念日。

items.example: The actor became a celebrity overnight.
There was a celebratory mood in the room.
Celebrare is the source of celebrate.
items.exampleCN: celebrare 是 celebrate 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Celebrare passed into English through French.
Celeber is the base of celebrity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: celeber 是 celebrity 的词基。

definition_en: a party or ceremony held to mark a special occasion, or the act of praising someone publicly
core_image: 人群聚在一处，为一件喜事举杯欢呼
scene: 小镇广场挂满彩灯。The whole village joined the celebration in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 celebration 指「庆祝活动」（第 1 个义项：为纪念喜事而举行的聚会）；句意是全村人都参加了广场上的庆祝活动。

senses.title: A party for a special occasion
senses.definition: a social event held to mark a happy occasion such as a birthday or a victory
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念生日、胜利等喜事而举行的社交活动
senses.example: The team held a celebration after the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛之后球队举行了庆祝活动。
senses.why: The Latin base meant a crowded gathering, and a party is that crowd in its most familiar form.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基意为人群聚集，而聚会正是这种人群最熟悉的形态。

senses.title: Public praise of someone
senses.definition: the act of praising a person or achievement openly in speech, writing or art
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、文字或艺术中公开赞扬某人或某项成就
senses.example: The film is a celebration of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片是对乡村生活的赞颂。
senses.why: A crowd that gathers to rejoice can also gather to praise, so the festive noun carries the honouring sense.
senses.whyCN: 为欢庆而聚集的人群也能为赞美而聚集，于是这个节庆名词也带上致敬义。

intro.en: Celebration is the noun of celebrate, built on a Latin word for a crowded gathering.
intro.cn: celebration 是 celebrate 的名词形式，词基是拉丁语中表示人群聚集的词。

items.en: Celeber meant crowded, busy or famous.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celeber 意为拥挤、繁忙或著名的。

items.en: Celebratio named a public gathering held to honour someone.
items.cn: celebratio 指为向某人致敬而举行的公众集会。

items.en: Celebration passed through French with the sense of solemn observance.
items.cn: celebration 经法语传来，带有庄严遵行的意味。

items.en: English celebration first names a religious observance and then any festive marking.
items.cn: 英语 celebration 先指宗教仪式，后指任何节庆纪念。

items.en: The word now covers birthdays, national holidays and praise expressed in art.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖生日、国庆以及艺术中的赞颂。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the -celebr- stem, while the meaning group lists other festive gatherings.
note.cn: 形近组保留 -celebr- 词干，近义组列出其他节庆聚会。

entries.definition: to mark a happy occasion
expressing joy at an event
a famous person
a day or period of public rejoicing
entries.definitionCN: 公众欢庆的日子或时期

entries.definition: a social gathering for pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 为消遣而举行的社交聚会

entries.definition: a formal series of acts on a special occasion

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the crowded root, the -tion noun ending and the fixed phrase in celebration of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拥挤词根、-tion 名词词尾以及固定搭配 in celebration of。

normal.en: Celebration is celebrate plus -ion, the event rather than the act.
normal.cn: celebration 就是 celebrate 加 -ion，指活动而非动作。

normal.en: The root celeber meant crowded, so a good celebration fills the room.
normal.cn: 词根 celeber 意为拥挤，所以好的庆典总把屋子填满。

normal.en: In celebration of is the phrase that links the noun to the reason for the party.
normal.cn: in celebration of 这个搭配把庆典与举办的理由连起来。

normal.en: A celebration of life praises a person rather than merely marking a date.
normal.cn: a celebration of life 是在赞颂一个人，而不只是记一个日子。

normal.en: The plural celebrations only adds an s, with the stress staying on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 复数 celebrations 只加 s，重音仍在第二个音节。

abstract.en: Picture lanterns strung across a square full of talking people.
abstract.cn: 想象彩灯横跨广场，下面全是交谈的人。

abstract.en: Picture a table crowded with dishes and raised glasses.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摆满菜肴、举着酒杯的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a choir singing in praise of an old teacher.
abstract.cn: 想象合唱团为一位老教师歌唱致敬。

examples.en: The wedding celebration lasted until midnight.
examples.cn: 婚礼庆祝活动一直持续到半夜。

examples.en: There were celebrations in the streets after the result.
examples.cn: 结果公布后街上到处是庆祝活动。

examples.en: The exhibition is a celebration of local craft.
examples.cn: 这场展览是对本地手工艺的赞颂。

dict_mnemonic.text: celebration 里有 celebrate：把「庆祝」这个动作变成一场活动，就成了庆典。

root: 源自拉丁语 celebratio（公众集会致敬），出自 celebrare，词基 celeber 意为拥挤、著名；与 celebrate 同根。

sensesIntro.en: A crowded gathering gives the party sense, and the same crowd turned toward praise gives the honouring sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 人群聚集给出聚会义，同一人群转向赞美则给出致敬义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd gathered around one happy event.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着一件喜事聚集的人群。

branches.en: A birthday or victory party keeps the festive sense.
branches.cn: 生日或胜利聚会保留节庆义。

branches.en: Praise in art turns the gathering into an act of honour.
branches.cn: 艺术中的赞美把聚会变成致敬行为。

branches.en: In celebration of fixes the link between party and reason.
branches.cn: in celebration of 固定了聚会与理由之间的联系。

branches.en: Both put a person or event at the centre of attention.
branches.cn: 两者都把人物或事件放在关注中心。

branches.en: The praise sense often appears in reviews and dedications.
branches.cn: 赞颂义常见于评论与献词中。

intro.en: Celebration keeps the -celebr- stem across verb, noun and adjective.
intro.cn: celebration 在动词、名词与形容词之间保留 -celebr- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin celebratio and celebrare are the direct ancestors of the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 celebratio 与 celebrare 是英语名词和动词的直接祖先。

items.exampleCN: 庆祝活动持续了好几天。
名气没给他带来多少安宁。

items.example: Celebrare is the verb behind it.

latinEntries.example: Celebratio passed into French and English.

definition_en: the smallest living unit of an animal or plant, a small room such as a prison room, or a device that stores electric power
core_image: 一个四面封闭的小格子
scene: 显微镜下能看到微小的结构。Each cell in the sample had a dark centre.
sceneCN: 这里 cell 指「细胞」（第 1 个义项：生物体最小的生命单位）；句意是样本里的每个细胞都有一个深色的中心。

senses.title: The basic unit of life
senses.definition: the smallest part of a living thing that can carry out the processes of life
senses.definitionCN: 生物体中能进行生命活动的最小单位
senses.example: A red blood cell carries oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 红细胞负责运送氧气。
senses.why: Early microscopists saw tiny walled compartments and borrowed the word for a small room.
senses.whyCN: 早期显微镜学家看到一个个有壁的小隔间，就借用了表示小房间的词。

senses.title: A small closed room
senses.definition: a small room, especially one in a prison or a monastery
senses.definitionCN: 小型房间，尤指监狱或修道院中的
senses.example: The prisoner paced his narrow cell.
senses.exampleCN: 犯人在狭窄的牢房里来回踱步。
senses.why: This is the original sense: a small enclosed room, from Latin cella.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：拉丁语 cella 所指的小型封闭房间。

senses.title: A unit that stores electric power
senses.definition: a container of chemicals that produces electricity, or one unit of a larger battery
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学物质产生电的容器，或电池组中的一节
senses.example: The torch needs a new cell.
senses.exampleCN: 手电筒需要换一节电池。
senses.why: Each battery unit is a sealed compartment, so the room word fits the small power box.
senses.whyCN: 每个电池单元都是密封的小格，于是房间用词正好套在这只电源小盒上。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room, and every later sense keeps the idea of a closed compartment.
intro.cn: cell 来自拉丁语 cella（小房间），后面每个义项都保留封闭小格的意思。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室或神庙内室。

items.en: Celle named a small room, especially a monk's chamber.
items.cn: 古法语 celle 指小房间，尤指修士的居室。

items.en: Cell covers small rooms in monasteries and prisons.
items.cn: 中古英语 cell 涵盖修道院和监狱的小室。

items.en: Microscopy applies the word to the tiny compartments seen in living tissue.
items.cn: 十七世纪显微镜学把该词用到活体组织中的微小隔间上。

items.en: Electricity adds the battery sense, and compounds such as cell phone spread the word further.
items.cn: 电学又添上电池义，cell phone 等复合词进一步推广该词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the room root through its derivatives, while the meaning group lists other enclosed spaces.
note.cn: 形近组沿房间词根经派生词展开，近义组列出其他封闭空间。

entries.definition: made of cells, or relating to mobile phones
entries.definitionCN: 由细胞组成的，或与移动电话有关的

entries.definition: a person who shares a prison cell
the substance forming plant cell walls
entries.definitionCN: 构成植物细胞壁的物质

entries.definition: a part of a building enclosed by walls
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物中被墙围起的一部分

entries.definition: a large room used for a special purpose
entries.definitionCN: 用于特定用途的大房间

entries.definition: one of several separate sections
entries.definitionCN: 若干分隔部分中的一格

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-room root, the blood and prison phrases and the -ular ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小房间词根、血液与监狱搭配以及 -ular 词尾。

normal.en: Cell is simply Latin cella, a small room, and every sense is still a little box.
normal.cn: cell 就是拉丁语 cella（小房间），每个义项都还是一个小盒子。

normal.en: A prison cell and a biological cell share one shape: a wall around a small space.
normal.cn: 牢房与生物细胞共享一个形状：围住小空间的墙。

normal.en: Cellular means made of cells, and also names the mobile phone network built from small areas.
normal.cn: cellular 意为由细胞组成，也指由小区域构成的移动电话网。

normal.en: Cellmate is cell plus mate, the person sharing that small room.
normal.cn: cellmate 是 cell 加 mate，同住那间小室的人。

normal.en: The plural cells is regular, and the word stays one syllable throughout.
normal.cn: 复数 cells 变化规则，整词始终只有一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny walled box seen through a microscope lens.
abstract.cn: 想象透过显微镜镜片看到的一个微小带壁盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow stone room with one high window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间窄小的石屋，只有一扇高窗。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal cylinder sliding into a torch.
abstract.cn: 想象一节小金属筒滑进手电筒。

examples.en: The disease attacks healthy cells in the blood.
examples.cn: 这种病攻击血液中的健康细胞。

examples.en: He spent three nights in a police cell.
examples.cn: 他在警局牢房里待了三晚。

examples.en: This lamp runs on a single cell.
examples.cn: 这盏灯只用一节电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: cell 读音短促，像把小盒子「塞」进口袋：细胞、牢房、电池都是一个个封闭的小格。

root: 源自拉丁语 cella（小房间、储藏室），经古法语 celle 进入英语，由房间义扩展到生物细胞与电池单元。

sensesIntro.en: A small room gives the prison sense, the microscope borrows the shape for life, and electricity borrows it again for power units.
sensesIntro.cn: 小房间给出牢房义，显微镜借这个形状指生命单位，电学又借它指电源单元。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small space shut in by walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面被墙围住的小空间。

branches.en: Monastery and prison rooms keep the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 修道院与监狱的房间保留最古老的义项。

branches.en: Microscopy transfers the walled box to living tissue.
branches.cn: 显微镜学把带壁盒子转移到活体组织上。

branches.en: Electricity seals chemicals inside a small cylinder.
branches.cn: 电学把化学物质封在小圆筒里。

branches.en: Both are tiny enclosed units separated from neighbours.
branches.cn: 两者都是与邻居隔开的小封闭单元。

branches.en: Both senses keep the physical container visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了可见的实体容器。

intro.en: Cell builds adjectives and nouns with -ular, -ulose and the compound mate.
intro.cn: cell 用 -ular、-ulose 以及复合成分 mate 构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cella also gives cellar and the first element of cemetery.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cella 也给出 cellar，以及 cemetery 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a small room or living unit

items.example: His cellmate taught him to read.
Her cell phone rang in the meeting.
The prison cell had no window.
Cella is the source of cell.
items.exampleCN: cella 是 cell 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cella 也是 cellar 的来源。
